summary: This continuation constructs the geometric circle method for polynomial maps to smooth affine hypersurfaces, with rank-Hankel arc strata, compact-support Fourier complexes, signed configuration-space first pages and monodromy parity. It separates independent dimension, polynomial-counting and prime-choice prefixes from the parent arithmetic estimates. Conservative comparison and irreducibility ranges are distinguished from unproved sharper targets. Explicit infinity-germ obstructions and controlled collars delimit a conditional, rather than unconditional, mapping-space degeneration argument.

declarations.provides: Evaluation of multivariate polynomials through a coefficient ring homomorphism and assigned variables; read declaration at pin.
Natural-valued matrix rank over a field, defined through the associated linear map; not a determinantal scheme.
Existing Hahn-series carrier with integer exponents; coefficient operations suffice for the finite residue expressions.
Valuation at infinity on rational functions: nonzero f/g has exp(deg f−deg g); its completion is already available in the same module.
In a commutative Noetherian ring, a proper ideal has height at most its span rank. The geometric componentwise dimension translation remains GCM.0.
For coprime residue and modulus, there is a prime above any bound in the prescribed class. Read the quantified theorem at the pin.
For distinct odd primes the product of the two Legendre symbols is the usual parity sign; p≡1 mod4 removes it.
For an odd prime p, the Legendre symbol of 2 is the character χ₈(p).
Spectral object in an abelian category with functorial connecting maps and exactness. It is a carrier; a finite localization filtration with its abutment is not supplied by this declaration.
Curries a continuous map X×Y→Z to a continuous map X→C(Y,Z) with the compact-open topology.
A nonempty locally closed subset of a Jacobson space meets the closed points.
A locally finite-type scheme over a Jacobson scheme is Jacobson.
The based fundamental group of the unit additive circle is multiplicatively equivalent to Z, with deck-endpoint convention fixed by the covering construction.

nodes.title: Affine dimension theorem for intersections
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, if irreducible closed Y,Z⊂A^M meet, each component C of Y∩Z has dim C≥dim Y+dim Z−M. For a closed V whose every component meets Z, dim(V∩Z)≤0 implies dim V≤M−dim Z. Independently, every component of the nonempty zero locus of r polynomials in A^M has dimension at least M−r.
proofSteps: Use the diagonal in A^M×A^M to express the intersection by M equations in Y×Z.
Apply the generalized principal ideal theorem componentwise and translate height to dimension for finite-type algebras over a field.
For the consequence choose a maximal-dimensional component of V; do not infer nonempty intersection from a dimension inequality.
acceptance: Two coordinate planes in A³ meet in a line and attain the bound.
Disjoint parallel lines do not satisfy the nonempty-intersection hypothesis.
For a cone, justify that every irreducible component contains the vertex before using the diagonal argument.

nodes.title: Degree-controlled projection for polynomial grids
nodes.statement: Let V⊂A^N over F_q(T) have dimension e≥0 and geometric total degree Δ, the sum of the projective degrees of its reduced geometric irreducible components. There is C(Δ,N), independent of q and the coefficients of V, such that for every nonempty finite subset S⊂F_q(T), #(V(F_q(T))∩S^N)≤C(Δ,N)|S|^e. Empty V contributes zero. Supply a degree-controlled projection/stratification or a direct finite-grid proof: the pieces and fibre bounds depend only on (Δ,N). A coordinate projection preserves polynomial strict height; any change of coordinates must carry an explicit height estimate. A merely generically finite projection is insufficient at exceptional fibres.
proofSteps: Audit the projection step of BV15 Lemma 2.8, separating finite fibres from a finite morphism and from generic finiteness.
Provide a degree-bounded stratification or a direct finite-grid degree lemma; prove the exceptional-locus estimates and uniform constants.
Record the unresolved proof audit as G1; no choice of generic linear coordinates with uncontrolled coefficients proves polynomialbox.

nodes.title: Degree-uniform polynomial point bound
nodes.statement: Let V⊂A^N over F_q(T) have dimension e≥0 and geometric total degree Δ (summing all reduced geometric components), with polynomial equations over F_q[T]. There is C(Δ,N), independent of q and the coefficients, such that for every integer h≥1 the number of u∈V(F_q[T]) with max_j |u_j|<q^h is at most C(Δ,N)q^(he), where |0|=0 and |a|=q^(deg a) for a≠0. Empty V contributes zero; for e=0 use the degree bound. For h≤0 only the zero vector can occur, and it contributes exactly when it belongs to V.
proofSteps: Identify the strict ball with polynomials of degree <h; each coordinate has q^h choices for positive integral h.
Apply the degree-controlled finite-grid/projection contract and sum its degree-bounded pieces.
Keep the BV15 finite-projection and height-uniformity audit open (G1); the inclusive radius q^N in that lemma corresponds to h=N+1.
acceptance: A coordinate affine e-plane has exactly q^(he) points in the strict positive-height box.
At h=0 nonzero constants are excluded; the count is zero or one.
A zero-dimensional variety has at most its degree many rational points regardless of h.

nodes.title: Choose a coefficient prime for fixed odd characteristic

nodes.title: Choose good residue characteristics for fixed coefficient prime
nodes.statement: For a fixed prime ℓ, integers B,k and finite bad-prime set S, there are arbitrarily large primes p>max(B,k,ℓ), p∉S, for which ℓ is a nonsquare modulo p and therefore has even multiplicative order. For odd ℓ choose a nonzero quadratic nonresidue a mod ℓ and the CRT residue p≡a mod ℓ, p≡1 mod4; for ℓ=2 use p≡5 mod8.
proofSteps: Choose the CRT unit class and use Dirichlet above every member of S.
For odd ℓ, quadratic reciprocity has positive sign because p≡1 mod4. For ℓ=2 use the supplementary law.
In a cyclic finite field unit group, an odd-order element is a square; conclude even order.
acceptance: The class 5 mod8 makes 2 a nonsquare.
For odd ℓ, a must be nonzero so the CRT class is a unit.
Avoidance is uniform over any prescribed finite set, not a single ad hoc characteristic.

nodes.title: Polynomial mapping scheme with a fixed leading vector
nodes.statement: Fix a field K, n≥2, k≥3, f∈K[x₁,…,x_n] of degree k, and a nonzero vector x with f₀(x)=0, where f₀ is the degree-k part. For d≥1 put g_j=x_jT^d+Σ_{0≤i<d}a_{i,j}T^i.
